answer: A harbor town stays honest when every new identity must dig a distinct marble pit on a distinct mesa terrace and polish each stone, while a distinct harbor-master weighs each polished marble at the quay. The first fake owes one marble, the second three, the third six, since the nth fake owes n times n plus one over two marbles, so the tenth fake alone owes fifty-five marbles and twenty fakes owe 1,540. Bulk farming fails because one digger works one pit at a time and each marble comes from one terrace only, like one quarryman hauling one marble slab down one mesa trail per tide.
